newsitem.title: USA: Mass. says lottery sales set new record of $3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Mass. says lottery sales set new record of $3 bln.

text.p: Massachusetts, whose budget gets a big boost from lottery sales, on Thursday said gross lottery sales set a new record in fiscal 1996, climbing 8.5 percent to $3.05 billion.

The state Treasurer, in prepared remarks, added that the lottery returned $662 million to the state, cities and towns, a 3.1 percent increase from the previous year, once payments for prizes, commissions, and expenses were deducted.
The state's budget was approximately $17 billion in 1996.

Joe Malone, the state Treasurer, pointed out that administrative expenses were reduced to 2.3 percent from 2.6 percent in fiscal year 1995, adding the national average is 8.2 percent. "We are continuing to look for new ways to improve on efficiency at the Lottery."

The Lottery's executive director, Sam DePhillippo, attributed the record growth to a 10 percent rise in Instant Ticket sales, which climbed to about $2 billion, and a 27 percent increase in Keno sales, which rose to $381 million.
